parts.name: Mesothelium (visceral peritoneum)
parts.description: Visceral peritoneal mesothelium at a specimen surface. Field boundaries are artificial sampling cuts; this is not the whole spleen.

parts.name: Capsule
parts.description: Connective-tissue capsule at the specimen surface; thickness is schematic. The cut face is an artificial observation window.

parts.name: Periarteriolar lymphoid sheath (PALS)
parts.description: T-cell-rich periarteriolar lymphoid sheath around an eccentric central arteriole; follicles bud alongside the sheath. Representative 3D human compartment relationships.

parts.name: Splenic follicles & mantle zone
parts.description: Curved B-cell-rich follicular mantle shells around responding germinal centres. Anterior portions are removed for inspection; follicles remain volumetric, not flat discs.

parts.name: Germinal centres
parts.description: Representative responding germinal centres. These are not present in every follicle and do not quantify immune activation. The section reveals their 3D nesting inside B-cell follicles.

parts.name: Perifollicular open spaces
parts.description: Selected discontinuous blood-filled extravascular spaces near human follicles; no endothelial marginal sinus or complete surrounding sinus ring.

parts.name: Superficial follicular zone (human)
parts.description: Selected superficial follicular tissue patches on the human follicle surface. This schematic does not impose a rodent-style concentric marginal-zone ring around PALS.

parts.name: Venous sinusoids (stave cells)
parts.description: Representative tortuous hollow sinus courses. Detailed longitudinal endothelial slits are resolved separately in the enlarged filtering inset; lumen calibre is schematic.

parts.name: Ring fibres
parts.description: External discontinuous basement-membrane hoops, exaggerated for readability. The enlarged inset shows their relationship to longitudinal staves.

parts.name: Trabeculae
parts.description: Branching connective-tissue trabeculae extend inward from the capsule; fitted passages carry vessels. There is no cortex-medulla subdivision.

parts.name: Trabecular artery
parts.description: Hollow representative trabecular artery supplying central arterioles. Open boundary port marks a sampled arterial entry, not a terminal capillary.

parts.name: Trabecular vein
parts.description: Hollow trabecular venous outflow with a specimen-boundary port; returns splenic blood toward the portal venous system.

parts.name: Central artery & follicular branches
parts.description: Hollow branching central arterioles follow eccentric PALS courses beside follicular B-cell compartments. These are sampled pathways, not complete vascular territories.

parts.name: Penicillar arterioles
parts.description: Sampled terminal arterial capillaries end openly in cords, without a tube bridging to a venous sinus. Human branch patterns and sheath presence vary.

parts.name: Sheathed capillaries (Schweigger-Seidel sheaths)
parts.description: Representative stromal/macrophage capillary sheaths surrounding selected capillary segments. Sheaths are not muscular arterioles and their exact functions remain under study.

parts.name: Pulp vein
parts.description: Hollow collecting pulp vein links the representative sinus outflow region to a trabecular vein. The field is not a complete perfusion atlas.

parts.name: Splenic cords (of Billroth)
parts.description: Limited anterior cutaway through a cohesive specimen matrix, with three-dimensional reticular scaffold and representative blood cells in splenic cords outside endothelial sinuses. Sparse fibres disclose relationships; they do not reproduce every cord cell. Open circulation exposes blood here before sinus re-entry.

parts.name: Inset: sinus endothelial staves
parts.description: Enlarged static detail. Longitudinal endothelial cells surround the sinus lumen; real gaps between adjacent staves represent interendothelial slits. Three anterior staves are removed as an artificial inspection window, not a normal defect. Shapes are illustrative, not measured cell mechanics.

parts.name: Inset: discontinuous basement-membrane hoops
parts.description: External ring-like basement-membrane support. The front portion is removed for inspection together with the window; thickness is exaggerated.

parts.name: Inset: extravascular cord reticular scaffold
parts.description: Sparse schematic support in the cord space outside the sinus. Tissue and blood occupy this extravascular compartment; this is not a closed vessel.

parts.name: Inset: red cells in cord space
parts.description: Biconcave red cells outside endothelial vessels in the open splenic cords. Cell size is exaggerated for explanation.

parts.name: Inset: flexible red cell at true stave gap
parts.description: One continuous closed deformed red-cell surface, with an external lobe and an intraluminal lobe connected by a narrow waist through an actual intact stave gap. Static illustrative geometry, not a computed mechanical simulation.

parts.name: Inset: red cells in sinus lumen
parts.description: Cells that have entered the sinus lumen return to venous circulation. The inspection window exposes the lumen.

parts.name: Inset: cord macrophage
parts.description: Cord macrophage clearing a retained cell. Mechanical retention and macrophage recognition are distinct steps; not every retained cell is automatically destroyed.

parts.name: Inset: macrophage nucleus
parts.description: Nucleus of the enlarged representative cord macrophage.

parts.name: Inset: rigid red cell retained for clearance
parts.description: Representative damaged or poorly deformable red cell retained outside the sinus and partly embraced by the macrophage. Opsonized-cell recognition may also drive clearance independently of stiffness.

parts.name: Inset: open terminal arterial capillary
parts.description: Hollow terminal capillary opens into the cords. Its mouth is not joined to the sinus: the intervening blood-filled extravascular space is the key open-circulation interval.

parts.name: Inset: patent venous outflow sleeve
parts.description: Open-ended hollow venous outflow sleeve continuous with the sinus lumen. Distal port is a specimen cut through the return route, not a physiological open arterial ending.
